comparator.name: Medicine
comparator.sourceNotes: Groningen combines the causes of disease and medical knowledge with training in consultation, professional practice, healthy ageing and research. This plan illustrates the Sustainable Care learning community. Students prepare their bachelor project in the first semester of year three and carry it out in the final semester.

routeSelection.basis: The generic Medicine target offers four Learning Communities for the Competency Development components while retaining one common medical-knowledge curriculum. Current official evidence does not identify one community as the broad default or academically dominant route. Sustainable Care is therefore selected neutrally because it is listed first in the 2026-2027 TER, without reference to UCR fit.

core: Biomedical foundations, disease mechanisms, physiology, anatomy, pharmacology and integrated medical knowledge
Diagnosis, treatment decisions and longitudinal clinical reasoning
Scientific training, epidemiology, statistics, evidence evaluation and medical research
Patient-centred health, behaviour, illness experience and shared decisions
Medical consultation, communication, teamwork and interprofessional collaboration
Prevention, healthy ageing, population health and healthcare innovation
Professional development, ethics, rights and responsibility
Supervised patient contact, care placements and physician competencies
adjacent: Patient health, behaviour and healthcare communication
Public health, prevention and healthy ageing
questions: How do biological mechanisms produce disease and treatment effects?
How do behaviour, communication and social context shape patient health and care?
How can prevention and population evidence support healthy ageing?

selection.assessment: Three related fields offer substantive, distinct responses to Groningen Medicine. Biomedical science has the strongest scientific overlap. Health psychology studies illness experience and interaction, and population health studies prevention and inequality. The professional and clinical curriculum remains a separate feature of Medicine.

alternatives.label: Biomedical science and disease research
alternatives.labelReason: The strongest UCR overlap is in cell biology, physiology, immunity, pathology, pharmacology and research methods.
alternatives.concept: Investigate what happens when cells, tissues and organs stop working normally. Build from anatomy, physiology and molecular biology to laboratory methods, infection, pathology, pharmacology and quantitative research.
progression: The life sciences foundation precedes cell biology, physiology, laboratory work and advanced disease courses. Mathematics precedes probability and numerical methods. Experimental methods support later research synthesis.

alternatives.label: Health psychology and communication
alternatives.labelReason: Health psychology, assessment and communication support the study of illness experience and health behaviour.
alternatives.concept: Explore how people experience illness and make decisions about health. Build from social psychology and brain science to health behaviour, psychological assessment, communication, teamwork and research on people’s experiences.
alternatives.distinctness: Differs from Biomedical science and disease research by 90 EC each way, with more psychology, communication and teamwork.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes health psychology and psychological assessment. Social psychology, behavioural economics and qualitative methods support later communication and teamwork.

alternatives.label: Population health, prevention and ageing
alternatives.labelReason: Epidemiology, social context, prevention and ageing organise this option.
alternatives.concept: Study why health and illness vary across populations and over a lifetime. Use epidemiology, social research and economics to examine prevention and inequality, including the effects of climate and environmental conditions.
alternatives.distinctness: Differs from Biomedical science and disease research by 90 EC and from Health psychology and communication by 52.5 EC each way, with more population methods, public policy and environmental justice.
progression: Introductory epidemiology, sociology and research methods precede work on prevention, health inequalities and public policy. Research Methods & Statistics precedes behavioural economics, public economics and econometrics.

trace: Introduces biomolecules, cellular structures and processes, genetics and the analysis of biological experiments.

blocks: Groningen combines human development, metabolism and clinical cases in an integrated block.
Both study neoplasms and processes underlying disease. Groningen also covers endocrine and blood disorders in clinical context.
Both study pathogens, immune responses and infection. Groningen integrates those topics with medical cases.
Both cover disease mechanisms in the heart and lungs. Groningen also studies clinical presentations and care.
Groningen trains students in medical consultation, professional practice, healthy ageing and research.
Both study brain function, including consciousness and cognitive processes. Groningen focuses on neurological presentations.
Both examine mood, anxiety and psychotic disorders. Groningen integrates the material with medical and psychiatric practice.

notes.text: Groningen teaches medicine through biological science, clinical reasoning, medical consultation and supervised care. The UCR options explore related academic fields and do not lead to physician qualification.

The UCR options do not include supervised patient care, clinical examination and treatment training, or Groningen’s medical progress tests. Groningen’s required bachelor project is assessed within its final competency block.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen Medicine studies the causes of disease and prepares students for medical practice through consultation training, supervised care and research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options explore disease mechanisms, health behaviour and population health. Groningen combines these subjects with training and assessment in clinical practice.
